Graduate Admissions
Thank you for your interest in our graduate program. All the basic information you need to complete an application to the NMSU graduate astronomy program is available on this web page and at NMSU Graduate Admissions.
The admissions process requires documents in electronic format. This includes application forms, personal statements, unofficial transcripts, and letters of recommendation.
* Note: The GRE General and GRE Physics exams are not required for NMSU Astronomy. They will not be considered if submitted with your application.
Applications
The deadline to start the graduate program in August 2027 is December 15, 2026.
Apply Now!
Required Materials - Deadline: December 15th
There are several components to a complete application:
Application to the Astronomy Graduate Program and the Graduate School with fee. (Note: There is no application fee if this is your first application to NMSU.)
Statement of Interest (1500 words, including 300 words describing why you are interested in NMSU specifically and including an AI Disclosure)
Transcripts
Three (3) Letters of Recommendation
(optional) CV
Details for each of these components are given below:
1) Application: For admission to the NMSU Astronomy Graduate Program, you must apply through the NMSU Graduate School electronic application system. Through that system (called SLATE) you will enter your personal data, list your recommenders, and upload documents.
2) Statement of Interest: In order to help us evaluate how you might fit into our department, please provide a brief description of your research interests (1500 words, including 300 words describing why you are interested in NMSU specifically and including an AI Disclosure). If you have direct experience with astronomical research, then tell us about the specific problem(s) that you have worked on, what your responsibilities were, what you learned from the process, and how this engagement inspired you to want to apply to graduate school. Also, let us know if you have experience writing papers, delivering presentations or posters, or attending meetings. Alternatively, if you have not been directly involved in research, please tell us which classes, instructors, or other experiences have inspired you to apply to our program. As you write, keep in mind that we are looking to understand how your interests and experiences might be a good match for NMSU’s research groups.
Required AI Disclosure: The use of AI tools (in particular, Large Language Models like ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) in writing the Statement of Interest is strongly discouraged, because we are interested in getting to know you, the applicant, as a person and as a potential future graduate student. The Statement of Interest must include an AI Disclosure indicating whether or not AI tools were used in the preparation of the document and, if yes, describing the extent and nature of their use. If an applicant is suspected to have used an AI tool but no AI Disclosure is included, this will negatively impact the evaluation of their application.
3) Transcripts: Include transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Unofficial transcripts are acceptable for the initial application; official versions are required for admitted candidates later in the process.
4) Three Letters of Recommendation: Please make sure to enter the names and contact information for three letter writers in your application. A notification will be sent to them by the system to submit their letters before the deadline.
5) A CV is not required, but is generally helpful, so feel free to upload one as a separate document.
Approximate Admissions Timeline
Application deadline (December 15): deadline for submitting applications and recommendation letters
First application update (late January): applicants are informed if they are declined, waitlisted, or being invited to do a remote interview
Second application update (mid February): applicants are informed if they are declined, waitlisted, or receiving an offer of admission
On-Campus Visit (mid March): potential campus visit for applicants with offers
Down-select date (April 1): applicants with multiple offers are strongly encouraged to select their top two choices and officially decline other offers
Decision date (April 15): deadline to accept initial offers
Contact and Correspondence
Please direct email messages regarding applications to astro-gradapps at nmsu.edu. A member of the Graduate Admissions Committee or another appropriate member of the Astronomy Department will respond promptly to all queries. If you send an email directly to a specific member of the department, please cc: the above account on your message. (This will help us to insure that all email messages receive a prompt response.)
Correspondence may include specific questions about our graduate astronomy program, assistance setting up direct contact with a current graduate student to learn about graduate life at NMSU, or any other related topic. If you wish to call or write to a specific person, please consider contacting one of the following individuals.

Researching the NMSU Astronomy Program
Each of our research groups is described on a central research page explaining the broad goals of the group and listing the group members. All research staff (faculty, students, postdocs) maintain an individual research page as well, describing the work that they do themselves (so you can read about many of the projects that we work on at NMSU by clicking on the names of people listed in the directory page).
Have a peek at all the exciting publications that department members have written.
The Observatories section will tell you about a number of the observatory facilities that NMSU astronomers often use.
The calendar lists talks that will be given in the department throughout the current semester (including our colloquium series with guest speakers, our weekly informal lunch talks, research group meetings, and the journal club astroph discussions).
The entries under the Public Open House heading provide an overview of public outreach efforts through the department.
The Directory pages also list phone numbers and email addresses for all department members so that they are easy to contact; don’t hesitate to call upon one of us if you have questions and you think that we can help.
